name: Barclays
summary: Barclays' interviews usually explore why you want the role and how your past examples show its five published Values: Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship. For early careers, Barclays describes short interactive online assessments, then an assessment centre that includes a motivational interview with a leader. Experienced hires usually have an online assessment or short phone interview before the main interview, and some roles add a case study, role play or presentation.
rounds: Early careers: two short interactive online assessments, plus a technical skills test for technical programmes
Experienced hires: online assessments or a short phone interview on your experience and skills
Assessment centre or interview, in person or virtual; for early careers it often has two or three stages, including a motivational interview with a leader
Some roles add a role play, case study or presentation
Screening checks after a successful interview, which depend on location
looks_for: A specific, well-researched reason for wanting this role at Barclays
Examples from your own experience that show the skills and behaviours in the job description

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made sure everyone in a group felt able to contribute.
covers: Who was being left out and how you noticed
What you changed in how the group worked
How the work or the decision improved as a result

questions.text: Tell me about a time doing the right thing took courage or cost you something.
covers: The situation and the pressure to take the easier route
What you did, and who you told
The outcome, and whether you would do it the same way again

questions.text: Describe a time you went out of your way to help a customer or colleague when it wasn't strictly your job.
covers: What they needed and why nobody else was picking it up
What you did, showing empathy rather than just following a script
The difference it made to them

questions.text: Tell me about something you left in better shape than you found it: a process, a project or a team.
covers: What state it was in when you took it on
The changes you made and how you got others on board
How it held up after you moved on

questions.text: Tell me about a time you set yourself a high standard and fell short. What did you change?
covers: The standard and why it mattered to you
Where and why you fell short, owned honestly
What you do differently now

questions.text: A customer calls because their card payment was declined while they were travelling. How would you help them?
covers: Verifying who they are without asking for their full PIN or passwords
Likely reasons in plain words: a fraud check, a limit, funds or wrong details
Fixing what you can on the call and explaining what happens next

questions.text: What does an investment bank do, and how is it different from a retail bank?
covers: Investment banking: advising on deals, helping companies raise money, trading for institutional clients
Retail banking: accounts, cards, loans and mortgages for individuals and small businesses
How the risks and sources of income differ, and where the role you want sits

questions.text: How would you design a system that flags possibly fraudulent card transactions within a second?
covers: Inputs: transaction details, device, location and the customer's usual pattern
Rules plus a scoring model, and the time budget for each step
Balancing false alarms against missed fraud, and learning from confirmed cases

questions.text: A report you own shows totals that don't match the finance team's figures. How would you work out which is right?
covers: Comparing definitions, data sources and cut-off times first
Reconciling a small sample line by line to find where they split
Agreeing the fix with finance and writing down the definition

questions.text: If a central bank raises its policy rate, what usually happens to savings rates, loan rates and a bank's customers?
covers: Banks' funding costs rise; variable loan and mortgage rates usually follow
Savings rates often rise too, sometimes more slowly
Effects on borrowing demand, customers who struggle to repay and the bank's margin

questions.text: How would you make sure a change to a banking app doesn't break payments for existing customers?
covers: Testing at several levels, including the payment journeys that matter most
Releasing gradually behind a switch, with monitoring and a quick way back
Keeping a record of the change for audit and incident review

questions.text: Why Barclays, and why this programme or team?
covers: Something specific about Barclays' business or the programme, not only its size
How the role matches what you've done and want to learn
What you've done to find out about it: events, people, reading

questions.text: Barclays' purpose is 'Working together for a better financial future'. What could that mean in the role you're applying for?
covers: The purpose in your own words
A concrete link to the day-to-day work of the role
A short example of something similar you have done

questions.text: Where would you like to be a few years after joining this programme?
covers: A realistic next step within the business
The skills you want to build to get there
Why Barclays is the right place to build them

tips: Learn the five Values and prepare two examples for each; Barclays says assessors look for alignment with its Values and ways of working.
Use the practice tests on Barclays' assessment platform before the online assessments; you can take them on a phone or tablet.
Prepare hard for the motivational interview: why Barclays, why this business area, and what you've done to learn about it.
Read the job description for the skills and behaviours it lists, and map one example from your experience to each.
Barclays says third-party AI tools, including transcription bots and meeting assistants, aren't permitted in its interviews, and using one gets the application withdrawn.
Ask your recruiter early if you need adjustments, such as extra time; Barclays offers them through the process.
